method:
Extraction used an existing tool, with no new C++ and no build. The tool is build-cpp/Release/hydra_replay.exe "score --chart <file> --difficulty <d> --prodrums 0|1 --bass2x 0|1" with no activations. Its JSON has one row per chord with an integer "tick" (the file's own ticks) and each note's colour and cymbal flag. It loads through load_songpath, the same loader the app uses, so flams, disco flip, dropped 2x kicks and Pro-off toms are already applied. Script: scratch corpus/extract.py, 6 threads, 1840 runs.

Hydra lists a chord's notes sorted by base score (Chord::notes(true)), not by lane. So I re-sorted each chord into lane order (kick, red, yellow, blue, green) before building the note list. Lane bits were kick 1, red 2, Y/B/G tom 4/8/16 and Y/B/G cymbal 32/64/128. Instrument was 9 with Pro on and 6 with it off.

Step 3 ran a byte-identical copy of probes/capped/shuffle_ref_capped.py (same SHA-256), imported from scratch so the repo got no __pycache__. A small note class records which notes the reference has already written. On a freeze, that names the note it hung on and the chord before it. Script: corpus/classify.py.

Step 4 re-ran every run with each chord's note order reversed, kick included. A run counts as changed if its status, its freeze tick or any note's output pad differs.

Three cross-checks. First, my harness fed the video chart reproduces all 22 video ticks. Second, an independent raw-file count (corpus/raw_pad_check.py) found at most 2 pad notes per tick on Expert, matching Hydra. Third, the one .chart with lower-difficulty sections but no notes has those sections empty in the file.

gaps:
No run in the corpus froze. Every run with notes finished: 1288 of 1288. The other 552 of the 1840 runs had no notes to shuffle. That is 46 charts that chart only Expert drums, times 3 lower difficulties, times 4 Pro/2x settings. They are real gaps in the files, not extraction failures, so extraction failed for 0 charts.

The corpus cannot test the four-colour freeze at all. No chord in any run has more than 2 pad notes. Across all runs, Hydra's chords break down as 290,336 kick-only, 1,033,196 with one pad and 245,672 with two pads. The raw Expert files agree: 100,784 ticks with one pad, 20,999 with two, none with three or more. So the four-colour case is untested here, not shown to be safe.

The corpus doesn't test seed zero either. The smallest seed in any run is 1152. Forty-eight runs start on tick 0, but each has a later note among its first four.

There were no same-colour clashes and no notes left with no pad, in the normal order or reversed. That only covers chords of up to 2 pads.

Reversing the order inside each chord changed the output of 1188 of 1288 runs. In 1168 of them, different pads show on screen. In 20, each chord shows the same pads but the notes are paired with them differently. 100 runs came out identical. In 254 runs the seed itself changes, because the four-note seed cut falls inside a chord. Those 254 runs come from 37 distinct charts, which is the figure in seed_cut_inside_chord. So open question 2 (the order of notes inside a chord) matters for almost every chart.

Four things this can't show. First, it uses Hydra's lane order. The game's real order is still open question 2. Second, it uses the file's own ticks, at 192 or 480 resolution. Whether the game rescales them is open question 1. Third, Hydra keeps only one note per lane per tick, so a 2x kick sharing a tick with a normal kick shows as one kick. Fourth, the extra note a flam adds is placed by Hydra's rules, not checked against the game.

The 2x Bass on/off split also matters only where a chart has 2x kicks. For every chart below Expert, the two runs are the same input.

question: Open 3: is the star base (0x20F4680, stored at engine+0x1D0) computed after the note builder 0x20D2EA0 has shuffled the notes, so the star cutoffs include cymbals the shuffle creates? Open 4: in 0x20F0C30 and 0x20F0B30, (i) is the redraw loop uncapped, (ii) is a zero seed special-cased, (iii) does anything upstream catch or avoid either freeze, and what would the user see?
answer:
Open 3: yes, settled. The star base runs after the shuffle, on the shuffled list. The star base function 0x20F4680 has exactly one direct caller in the whole binary: the engine base constructor 0x20F79E0. That constructor takes the note builder's result struct as its first argument, copies it into engine+0x1E0, and then calls the star base, which walks the note list at engine+0x1E0 (the struct's first field) and reads each note's lane mask at note+0x80, the same field the shuffle writes. The chain that gets there is BasePlayer slot 46 (0x208870): it calls the note builder 0x20D2EA0 (which calls the shuffle at 0x20D3315 for drums when modifier bit 0x40 is set, before it packs the list into the result struct), and only then calls the engine factory (slot 41, DrumsPlayer 0x33C560) with that struct; the factory constructs the drums engine (0x20DF680 -> 0x100EAE0 -> 0x20F79E0), which calls the star base. So the game's star cutoffs count cymbals created by the shuffle (each cymbal adds 15 to the per-note base, r13 = 0x0F when the cymbal check 0x214BE30 says yes). Hydra computing the base from the shuffled chart matches the game; nothing extra is needed.

Open 4 (i): confirmed. The drum redraw loop is 0x20F10E0 to 0x20F1131: call the lane draw, build the blocked-pad mask from the previous chord's output, `test dx, ax; jne 0x20F10E0`. There is no counter, no timer, no fallback branch. The only way to skip the draw is the copy rule at 0x20F0FCD-0x20F0FDE (pattern two chords back is nonzero and equals this chord's pattern). A chord that used all four colours blocks every pad (the mask at 0x20F110A-0x20F112B folds toms and cymbals to colours, so 0x1E becomes 0xFE), so the next chord's first note redraws forever unless the copy rule fires. The lane draw 0x20F0B30 itself loops only until it has drawn `count` distinct lanes; a drum note holds one lane, so it always returns after one draw for drums. (Guitar, out of scope: its loop at 0x20F10F7 redraws while the result equals the previous output, also uncapped.)

Open 4 (ii): confirmed. The seed is the sum over the first min(4, count) notes of mask*tick (0x20F0D90-0x20F0DB9). The generator object is built inline at 0x20F0DBF-0x20F0DE8: allocate, call an empty base constructor (0x6D60 is just `ret`), store seed<<3 at +0x10 and seed>>3 at +0x18. No test for zero anywhere. In 0x20F0B30 the xorshift step with state (0,0) yields 0, so trunc(0)+1 = lane 1 = bit 0x2 (red) every time. With four notes on tick 0 the seed is 0, the first pad note gets red, and the second pad note (same chord or next chord, since red is then in the blocked mask) redraws forever. The copy rule cannot save the second chord because the pattern two back is still 0.

Open 4 (iii): no catch or avoidance found; partly open. The shuffle is called directly and synchronously inside the builder, the builder directly inside BasePlayer slot 46, and slot 46 directly from GameManager methods (0xB5220, 0xBA8B0, 0xBD640) and a GameManager UniTask state machine (0xD9EF0). None of these listings references a thread-pool switch, a timeout, or a watchdog. An infinite loop is not an exception, so no handler applies. The chord pattern function just ORs the chained notes' masks; no chord-size cap is visible in the builder's call sequence. A second path also runs the builder with the player's modifiers: GlobalVariables 0x235AD0 (the online score path, strings "Failed to load song object for" and "Error loading song into memory:"), from a UniTask in the leaderboard class; it would hang the same way. What the user would see: Unity runs these on the main thread, so the game stops responding at the point it loads the chart (loading screen or song start), with no error and no crash; Windows reports "not responding" and the process has to be killed. This last sentence rests on Unity's threading model plus the absence of a thread switch in the listings, not on a game run.
evidence: 0x20F7DCC: `call 0x1820F4680` in the engine base ctor 0x20F79E0, the only direct call site of the star base in .text (callers.txt); the result goes to engine+0x1D0 at 0x20F7DEB (`mov [rsi+0x1D0], eax`).

0x20F7BE0-0x20F7C55: the ctor copies 0xA0 bytes from its struct argument (rdi) into engine+0x1E0; dump.cs line 530043 says engine+0x1E0 is the builder's result struct type, and line 528228 says that struct's field +0 is the note list.

0x20F473A: star base loads `rdx = [rbx+0x1E0]` (the list) and enumerates it; 0x20F4849 reads `word ptr [rdi+0x80]` (lane mask), and 0x20F480F calls the cymbal check 0x214BE30 to set the +15 (r13 = 0x0F) per note.
0x20F1151: the shuffle writes `word ptr [r14+0x80], r15w` (the new lane mask), the same field the star base reads.

0x208986: BasePlayer slot 46 (0x208870) calls the note builder 0x20D2EA0; 0x208AAF then calls vtable slot 41 (`call [rax+0x3C8]`) with the result struct; dump.cs line 10089 says DrumsPlayer 0x33C560 is the slot-41 override taking that struct and returning the engine; callers4.txt: 0x33C9BA calls the drums engine ctor 0x20DF680, which calls 0x100EAE0 at 0x20DF736, which calls 0x20F79E0 at 0x100EB63.
0x20D3306-0x20D3315: in the builder's drums branch, `test bl, 0x40; jbe skip; call 0x20F0C30` with rcx = the note list; 0x20D364E builds the result struct from that list afterwards.

0x20F10E0-0x20F1131: redraw loop: `call 0x20F0B30` (lane draw), fold the previous output into a colour-blocked mask (0x20F110A-0x20F112B), `test dx, ax; jne 0x20F10E0`. No counter, no time check, no other exit.
0x20F0FCD-0x20F0FDE: copy rule gate: `mov eax,[rsp+0x28]; test ax,ax; je draw; cmp ax,r13w; jne draw` (pattern two chords back must be nonzero and equal).

0x20F0D90-0x20F0DB9: seed loop, `movzx ecx,[rax+0x80]; imul rcx,[rax+0x40]; add rdi,rcx` over up to 4 notes; 0x20F0DBF-0x20F0DE8: new object, empty ctor (0x6D60 is `ret`), `lea rcx,[rdi*8]; mov [rbx+0x10],rcx; shr rdi,3; mov [rbx+0x18],rdi`. No zero check.
0x20F0B73-0x20F0BEB: xorshift step and lane = trunc(r * 2^-31 * (N-1)) + 1; with state 0 this is lane 1 every call, bit 0x2 (red).
0x20F0F71-0x20F0F9D: draw count = popcount(note+0x80), so one per drum note; 0x20F0C10 `cmp eax, edi; jl` ends the lane draw once that many distinct lanes are drawn.

vcalls_slot46_0x418.txt: slot-46 call sites in GameManager 0xB5220 (0xB5713), 0xBA8B0 (0xBAF6E), 0xBD640 (0xBDD21) and the GameManager UniTask MoveNext 0xD9EF0 (0xDA61A); none of those listings references a thread-pool switch, timeout or watchdog.

0x235C9E: GlobalVariables 0x235AD0 also calls the builder, with the settings struct built at 0x235C64 whose +4 (modifiers, per settings_ctor_2164780.asm) comes from the player's profile (`[r9+0x14]` at 0x235C2A); called from the leaderboard class's UniTask 0x3BD710.
implication_for_hydra: Open 3: keep the plan's design. Hydra computes the star base from the engine's totals on the shuffled chart, which is exactly what the game does; no second unshuffled base field is needed and the Stars tab needs no change beyond the shuffle itself. Open 4: both freeze cases are real in the code, with no cap or fallback, so Q5's rule (no path, with a sentence saying Clone Hero freezes loading the chart) is the right shape. Hydra's reference must keep the two conditions exactly as the code has them: the blocked mask folds toms and cymbals to colours and comes from the whole previous chord's output; the copy rule is the only escape and only fires when the chord two back has the same pattern. A capped loop in Hydra would invent a chart the game never shows.
game_test_needed: Two short game tests by the user, as the plan says: a three-chord chart with a four-colour chord then a lone snare, and a chart with four notes on tick 0, each with Note Shuffle on. Expected: the game stops responding at song load (no error, no crash). If either plays, the decode is wrong somewhere and the reading must be redone. For Open 3 a results screen with stars from a shuffled run would confirm the base, but the code reading is already unambiguous.
gaps: Three things were not proven by code. First, that no caller of the GameManager methods or the UniTask state machines runs them on a worker thread; I checked only the listings named here for thread-switch references, so the exact on-screen symptom (frozen main thread versus a loading spinner that never ends) rests on Unity's default threading. Second, the drum pre-transform functions were not re-audited for a chord-size cap; the chord pattern function and the builder's call sequence show none, and the game plays four-pad chords, so a cap is very unlikely. Third, the star-base call site count comes from a scan of direct call and jmp instructions; an indirect call through a method pointer would be missed, but the function is private and non-virtual (dump.cs line 530105), so none is expected.

question: Open 1: are ticks rescaled before the Note Shuffle seed is taken? Is the tick the seed reads (game note + 0x40) the file's raw tick for both .chart and .mid, and is it an integer?
answer: No rescaling. The tick the seed reads is the file's own tick, kept as a 64-bit integer, for both formats. The .chart reader parses the number before "= N" as a plain decimal into a 64-bit integer and stores it on the note untouched. The .mid reader sums each track's delta-time VLQs into a running 64-bit tick and stamps every event with it; the note builder copies the note-on event's tick onto the note untouched. The game note the shuffle sees gets that same value copied into its +0x40 field by the game-note constructor. The chart's resolution (the .chart "Resolution" value, or the MThd division) is stored separately in the song as a double (default 192.0) and is used for HOPO/sustain thresholds and tick-to-seconds conversion, never to scale a tick. So the seed is lane bits times raw file ticks at whatever resolution the file uses; a 192 .chart and a 960 .mid both shuffle from their own raw ticks. .sng/.srb were not traced separately, but every note in the game is created by one note-init function, which stores the tick it is handed unchanged.
evidence: 0x20F0DB1 (shuffle, scout-flag/shuffle_20f0c30.asm line 85): `movzx ecx, word ptr [rax+0x80]; imul rcx, qword ptr [rax+0x40]` - the seed multiplies the lane bits by a 64-bit integer read from game note + 0x40.

0x214BF57 (game-note ctor, gamenote_ctor_214BF10.asm): `mov rax, [rsp+0x78]; mov [rdi+0x40], rax` - the 5th constructor argument (a long) is stored at +0x40 with no arithmetic. The same ctor stores the double start time at +0x28 and end time at +0x30, so time and tick are separate fields.

0x20D4FA0 and 0x20D4FC8 (per-player note builder, build_gamenote_20D4BE0.asm): `mov r14, [rsi+0x10]` then `mov [rsp+0x28], r14` - the song-model note's +0x10 long is passed as that 5th argument unchanged. The time arguments come from `0x212B9C0` (song tick-to-seconds) called on the same +0x10 value.
0x214D27B (song-note init, songnote_init_214D240.asm): `mov [rbx+0x10], rbp` where rbp = rdx = the tick argument; +0x18 = length, +0x20 = lane, +0x24 = flags. No scaling.

.chart: 0x213B03B-0x213B052 (chart_line_parse_213AFC0.asm): `lea eax,[rdx-0x30]; lea rsi,[rsi+rsi*4]; lea rsi,[rsi-0x18]; lea rsi,[rdx+rsi*2]` - decimal accumulate rsi = rsi*10 + digit into a 64-bit register; returns (char, long).

.chart: 0x213D38A and 0x213D473-0x213D483 (trackbuilder_dispatch_213D2D0.asm): `mov rbp, [rax+8]` (the parsed tick) ... for 'N' lines `mov r8, rbp; call 0x213D620`. Also checks ordering with the string 'A track event occuring at offset {0} is out of order'.
.chart: 0x213D845 (trackbuilder_addnote_213D620.asm): `mov [rsi+0x10], r13` where r13 = r8 = the tick - stored on the pooled note unchanged.

.chart resolution: 0x2164510-0x2164580 (chart_resolution_2164100.asm): parses the number after 'Resolution', `cvtsi2sd xmm1, rdx; call 0x212C0B0` (song resolution setter). It then sets song+0x118 (HOPO threshold) from the resolution and song+0x114 (sustain cutoff). No tick is touched.

Song resolution setter 0x212C0E9-0x212C101 (song_set_resolution_212C0B0.asm): `movups [rcx+0xb0], xmm1` (writes the double to +0xB0 and +0xB8) then `[rcx+0xb0] = settings.float(+0x14) * resolution`. Song ctor 0x212ED9C-0x212EDB9 defaults both to 192.0 (0x4068000000000000).

.mid: 0x2155DD4-0x2155DED (midi_reader_2155C00.asm): `movzx eax, word ptr [rax+0x12]; cvtdq2pd xmm1, xmm1; call 0x212C0B0` - the MThd ushort becomes the song resolution. 0x2155E0E-0x2155EAC derive HOPO (res/3+1 or res*0.5+1) and sustain cutoff from it.

.mid: 0x214FA4B-0x214FADA (mtrk_read_214F6D0.asm): `call 0x213B340` (read VLQ delta), clamp negatives to 0, `add qword ptr [rax+0x20], rdx` (running 64-bit tick on the track), then `mov r9, [rax+0x20]; mov [rbx+0x10], r9` on the new event. Events carry raw summed ticks.

.mid: 0x2156D55-0x2156D6B and 0x2156FF1-0x2157002 (midi_track_handler_2156990.asm): `mov r12, [rsi+0x10]` (note-on tick), `mov rcx, [rax+0x10]` (paired note-off tick), `sub rdx, r12` (length); later `mov r9, [rsp+0x80]; mov r8d, esi; mov rdx, r12; call 0x20CEC60`. The only shift in the whole handler is `shl sil, cl` for a lane bit; there is no imul/cvt on ticks.

.mid: 0x20CED08-0x20CED0E (midi_sink_20CEC60.asm): `mov rdx, r14; call 0x214D240` where r14 = rdx = the tick from the handler; this function is a byte-for-byte twin of the chart's add-note 0x215BBF0 (same pool get, same length clamp against song+0x114).

Every function that takes a note from the note pool (fxref data ref 0x3cfabb0, note_pool_users.txt): the .chart track builder 0x213D620, the chart add-note 0x215BBF0, the MIDI twin 0x20CEC60 (mislabelled under the 0x2095040 cctor in names.pkl), and three functions of a Stream-based reader. All go through note init 0x214D240 or write +0x10 the same way.
implication_for_hydra: Hydra's current behaviour is right: keep the file's own ticks (a .mid at its header division, a .chart at its Resolution) and feed them to the shuffle seed as integers. No conversion to a fixed resolution is needed or wanted. The seed must be computed with 64-bit integer wraparound (unsigned long), because the game multiplies a 16-bit lane mask by a 64-bit tick and adds in 64-bit; Hydra's tick type must not be a float or a 32-bit int. For .sng/.srb, Hydra's unpack-to-.chart/.mid path matches the game because the game's notes all pass through the same note-init with the parsed tick.
game_test_needed: Optional confirmation only: the tiny groove from the plan saved as a 192-resolution .chart and a 960-resolution .mid, played with Note Shuffle on, should match the reference fed raw ticks. If either fails, the problem is elsewhere (note order, Open 2), not tick scaling.
gaps: Three things were inferred rather than read. (1) The MThd field at +0x12 is taken as the division (ticks per quarter) because it is the ushort passed to the resolution setter; the MThd parse method 0x211AF60 was not read. (2) The settings float at +0x14, which the setter multiplies into song+0xB0, was not identified (SongEntry passes it); it never touches a tick, so it cannot change the seed. (3) A Stream-based reader class (0x20E36F0, 0x20E4E90, 0x20E5130, 0x20E6160, created from 0x20F2190 via CliGameLauncher) also builds notes through the same note-init; its role (a binary chart cache or similar) and the writer that feeds it were not traced. If the game plays from such a cache, the ticks in it are whatever the parsers above stored, so the answer stands unless the cache writer rescales, which was not checked. .sng/.srb container unpacking was not traced; both land in the same two readers.

question: Open 2: what order are the notes in inside a chord? (a) sorted by lane or file order in the list the shuffle walks; (b) does the chord chain (+0x10/+0x18) match; (c) where the extra flam note goes; (d) a 2x kick (MIDI 95) on the same tick as a normal kick; (e) do kicks count in the four-note seed.
answer:
Short version: the game throws the file order away. Every chord is sorted by pad, kick first, then red, yellow, blue, green. That is the same walk Hydra already does. The three things Hydra must add are: put a flam's extra note right after its source note (not in pad order), merge a 2x kick and a normal kick on one tick into one kick that counts as a 2x kick, and count kicks in the seed.

(a) Sorted by pad, kick first. When a track is parsed (both the .mid and the .chart parser end in the same track finalizer, 0x215C320), the finalizer takes each run of notes on one tick and bubble-sorts it by note type ascending (KickDrum 13, RedDrum 14, YellowDrum 15, BlueDrum 16, then green), ties by the flags word ascending. The sort is stable and only swaps when strictly greater. Cymbal is a flag on the note, not a type, so a yellow cymbal sorts in the yellow slot. The per-player builder (0x20D4BE0) walks that finalized list in order and makes one play note per source note, so the list the shuffle walks is kick, red, yellow, blue, green for every chord. The flags tie-break only matters for two notes of the same pad on one tick, and those are merged into one note anyway (see d). The cached binary form of a chart stores the finalized list and only re-runs the chord indexer, so the order survives caching. One wrinkle that does not change the answer: the parsers store 4-lane green as type 18 (named OrangeDrum) and 5-lane green as 17; both sort after blue, and Hydra has no 5-lane drums.

(b) Yes. The builder links the chain in the same loop and the same order: a note whose chord-start index (+0x2c) differs from its own index (+0x28) gets prev = the play note made just before it, and that note gets next = the new one. The chord indexer sets +0x34 = 1 for every drum note, so the chord-head helper (0x214C9E0) returns the note itself and nothing is skipped. The kick is the chain head when present. The chord pattern function (0x214BCD0) ORs the masks walking next to the end, then prev to the start, so from any note it sees the whole chord, kick included (the shuffle masks the kick bit off).

(c) The flam copy is inserted at list index i+1, directly after its source note and before the remaining notes of that chord. Rule (0x20EF450): the source must be a single non-kick pad with the flam flag (play flag bit 17). Red gets a yellow-tom copy; yellow tom gets a blue-tom copy; blue tom gets a green-tom copy; green tom turns the source into a blue tom and the copy is a green tom; yellow cymbal gets a blue-cymbal copy; blue cymbal gets a green-cymbal copy; green cymbal turns the source into a blue cymbal and the copy is a green cymbal. The source gets flags |= 3. The copy is built with the copy constructor (0x214BE70), which copies tick, time, mask, flags and both chain pointers, then source.next = copy and copy.prev = source. The copy's next is the old next (copied), but the old next's prev still points at the source; that is an inconsistency in the game's chain, harmless for the shuffle because the pattern is computed from the chord's first note walking forward. The flam runs before the 2x-kick drop, the disco flip, the cymbal fold and the shuffle, so the copy is in the list the shuffle walks and counts toward the seed.

(d) Both parsers emit two separate KickDrum notes. In .mid, note numbers 95 and 96 both map to KickDrum (table at 0x210D824, case 0 -> 13), and 95 (also 83, 71, 59) gets the DoubleKick flag (8) from the bitmask 0x1001001001 at 0x21555D9. In .chart, N 0 is KickDrum with flags 0 and N 32 is KickDrum with DoubleKick (0x213D799). Neither parser dedups at insert. The finalizer then sorts the two kicks (normal first, since flags 0 < 8, unless the normal kick carries a ghost/accent bit, which is larger), merges their flags as a union into the longer note (the first on equal length, 0x215B8C0), and deletes the other (0x5DB0C0, key = type). The result is one kick note that carries DoubleKick. With 2x Bass off, 0x20EFF60 removes every note with that flag, so the tick has no kick at all. With 2x Bass on there is one kick. File order does not matter in the game; it only matters in Hydra today, which keeps the first of the two.

(e) Yes. The seed loop (0x20F0D90-0x20F0DBD) sums mask * tick over the first min(4, count) list entries with no lane test. Because kicks sort first in their chord, a chord's kick is the earliest of its notes in the seed. The list at that point already has flam copies inserted and, with 2x Bass off, 2x kicks removed (both run before the shuffle in 0x20D2EA0).

What Hydra must reproduce: walk each chord kick, red, yellow, blue, green (a cymbal sits in its pad's slot); insert a flam's copy immediately after its source with the lane rule above; when a tick has both a normal and a 2x kick, keep exactly one kick, flagged 2x, with the union of ghost/accent marks (so it disappears with 2x Bass off and is one kick with 2x Bass on); build the seed from the first four notes of that list, kicks and flam copies included. No parser change is needed for file order, because the game keeps none.
evidence: 0x215C040 (f215c040.asm) + 0x215E020 (f215e020.asm): for each run of equal tick ([note+0x10]) the finalizer slices the span and bubble-sorts it; the compare at 0x215E0A5-0x215E0C5 swaps when prev.type (+0x20) > cur.type, or types equal and prev.flags (+0x24) > cur.flags. Stable, ascending by (type, flags). Shows chords are sorted by pad, not file order.

dump.cs line 546901-546906 and 530349: source note type enum KickDrum=13, RedDrum=14, YellowDrum=15, BlueDrum=16, GreenDrum=17, OrangeDrum=18; flags enum DoubleKick=8, Tom=16, Cymbal=32, Flam=256, Ghost=512, Accent=1024. Cymbal is a flag, so cymbals sort with their pad.

implication_for_hydra: Hydra's lane walk (kick, red, yellow, blue, green) already matches the game's order inside a chord, so no parser change is needed to remember .mid note-on order or .chart line order; the game keeps neither. The shuffle pass must build its note list in that walk order, treating a cymbal as sitting in its pad's slot. Three extras: (1) the flam copy must be inserted directly after its source note, not in pad order, using the game's lane rule (red -> yellow copy, yellow -> blue, blue -> green, green -> source becomes blue and copy is green, and the same up the cymbals), and it has to exist before the seed is taken. (2) A tick with both a normal kick and a 2x kick must become one kick flagged 2x, carrying the union of ghost/accent marks, regardless of which came first in the file; with 2x Bass off that tick then has no kick, with 2x Bass on it has one. That differs from Hydra today, which keeps whichever of the two came first (song.cpp:927); it is the open item in memory derivation-audit-2026-10-03 and should be fixed as part of this work, since it changes which notes exist before the seed. (3) The seed uses the first four notes of that list, kicks and flam copies included, after 2x kicks are dropped when 2x Bass is off. The 2x-kick finding changes stored results (Dynamics totals and paths on charts with both kicks on one tick), so it is a user decision before any code.

Open 3: settled, yes. The star base 0x20F4680 has one caller in the whole binary, the engine base ctor 0x20F79E0, which first copies the builder's result struct into engine+0x1E0 and then calls the star base. The star base walks the struct's note list and reads each note's lane mask at note+0x80, and its cymbal test is just `mask & 0xE0`. The shuffle writes that same field. The chain is: BasePlayer slot 46 runs the builder (which shuffles the list in place when modifier bit 0x40 is set and the instrument is Drums=6 or ProDrums=9), then calls the engine factory with the struct, which reaches the engine ctor and the star base. So the game's star cutoffs use the shuffled notes. Hydra computing the base from the shuffled chart matches the game.
